City review fixes: ground shared with the terrain dressing, walkable stairways, closed golden-path frontage, sliced streaming, lazy colliders

- Terrain dressing: game.city.coversGround / ownsTrees tell dress.ts which ground the city dresses
  itself (detail area minus landmarks and river; blocks, streets, walls, aqueducts and fora beyond);
  no more grass through paving or shop floors, no doubled trees (two tiny hooks in dress.ts). The
  city steps the physics world once before its street graph, so ray probes see the static colliders.
- Detail area now also covers the golden-path corridors (+150 m): the Via Appia suburb at the spawn
  is real streets and blocks, not far massing.
- Stairways: stairProfile gives a walking surface never steeper than 0.66 that reaches the ground at
  both ends (the Centum Gradus now starts at the street below the cliff); flights on substructures,
  parapets open at road crossings. Parked carts only on level open ground. Ground cover never inside
  a block's outline nor on grades over 0.4. The real Actor walks every atlas stairway in tests.
- Golden path: piazza lots become shops, frontage gaps get shop rows or compound walls with gates,
  corridor yards and scraps are cobbled (corridor frontage closure ~0.6 -> ~0.97, tested).
- Streaming: block levels are built as jobs of small units (fill.ts, a unit-wise port of fillBlock),
  within a 5 ms frame budget, ordered by a 2 s look-ahead; the 183 s walk to the Rostra has no frame
  over 33 ms (was 78 over 33, 20 over 50).
- Physics: far-massing, tree, wall and aqueduct colliders exist only near the player
  (ProximityColliders): ~1.5k city colliders instead of ~13k.
- Memory / renderer: batch capacity grows by 1.25x and is trimmed back when geometry streams out
  (capacity after a walk 10.2M -> 4.8M vertices); batches draw with the pool's own copies of the
  library materials (no batched/plain program thrash), unsorted; mid-level batches are tagged and
  lose their shadows when a frame passes 2.45M triangles.
- Street graph: every link it makes is the nearest walkable one (plan raster: blocks, river, walls,
  street furniture, tree trunks, stairway sides; physics: walls, parapets, podia, slopes); nodes
  inside colliders move out, roads running into a monument's pier get a detour node, market stalls
  leave aisles. Probe and link tests.
- Docs: docs/modules/city.md (ground sharing, detail area, streaming, shadow budget, graph links,
  new numbers).

Merge river district review fixes + Cloaca walk-in parapet gap (worktree-wf_23b2142f-69d-8)

Quay parapet stays open beside the Cloaca outfall so its flight is walkable from the quay

After merging the terrain module's quay parapets, the Cloaca Maxima outfall's flight of steps
(on the bastion's flank, just outside the water module's +-3.2 m wall gap) had its head walled off
by the new parapet: the walk-in test ended on the quay 2.5 m above the landing, and the same was
true in a real boot (a horizontal ray across the flight head hit the parapet 1.2 m in).

The water module's other opening for landmarks, the `occupied` physics probe, never fires in the
game: Rapier ray queries only see colliders added before the last world step, and the game does
not step during setup, so the landmark's colliders are invisible to the probe (reproduced in a
test world with the game's build order and no step). The scenes that build the water before the
landmarks (terrain, landmark) could not use it either.

Fix, data instead of a probe: the parapet stays open QUAY.gapFlank (2 m) beyond each opening in
the face, on both sides. That covers the flight (to 5.0 m from the outfall axis) in any build
order; the quays keep their parapets everywhere else. Adds a test that the parapet is open across
the gap and its flanks and resumes at their edges, and notes the mechanism (and the inert probe)
in the terrain and river module docs.
